cultural.vision_reason: The picture shows an elaborately carved wooden chair/throne covered top to bottom with dozens of small carved human figures in scenes and rows, exactly matching a Chokwe chief's ceremonial throne with sculpted figural programme.

physical.title: Ceremonial Chair or Throne (citwamo ca mangu)
physical.summary: This citwamo ca mangu chair bears over 40 sculpted figures arranged in complex compositions across the chair’s top rail (back), stretchers (rungs), and legs; all symbolize the power of Chokwe supreme chiefs. Such chairs typically bear a dozen or fewer figures. Scenes of royal life and power wrap around the seat, reinforcing how the chief and his family are at the center of their polity and its business.

raw.did_you_know: Starting around the 1500s, Chokwe and other African leaders and traders received fine chairs as gifts from Portuguese traders. Chokwe leaders adapted this symbol of power as their own, using it in tandem with stools, an earlier kind of prestige seat.

cultural.vision_reason: A wooden three-pronged comb topped with a carved figure playing a drum, a classic Chokwe decorative art form for female patrons, matching the museum's own description and attribution.

physical.title: Comb
physical.summary: Several combs demonstrate a diversity of form and treatment. One (1976.180), a vigorously carved work showing a powerful drummer in performance, is an excellent example of Chokwe artistry meant for female patrons.

cultural.vision_reason: A classic wooden Pwo mask with woven-cap-style coiffure, arched eyebrows, diamond scarification, and metal earring—a well-known Chokwe mask type used by traveling dancers, matching the described "Pwo" mask from Sandoa, Katanga.

men använts med en virkad eller knuten trikå av svarta och vita tvinnade snören av jute eller annan fiber. Symbol. kvinnan.

Wooden mask, so-called "Pwo". This type of mask is used by travelling dancers. This mask has however been hanging in the "lupangu"=home of the dancers. The mask has been missing a wig, but has been used with a crocheted or knotted tricot made of black and white twinned strings of jute or another fibre. Symbol. The woman. Lit: Marie-Louise Bastin: Art Decoratif Tshokwe, II, pp. 380 ss. fig. 250. 250-264. 
Width: 17 cm, Thickness: 7 cm, Height: 24 cm.
Origin: Sandoa, South Katanga,  Rep of Congo-Kinshasa.
Ethnic group: tschokwe (chokwe) (utställningstext Horisonter - röster från ett globalt Afrika)
